Issues.Title: Fix issue 15345: TreeView OwnerDrawText Flickering even in TVS_EX_DOUBLEBUFFER
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes #15345

## Root Cause

In OwnerDrawText mode, TreeView always requested CDRF_NOTIFYPOSTPAINT, even when the native custom-draw notification contained an empty paint rectangle. With TVS_EX_DOUBLEBUFFER, this caused unnecessary post-paint drawing and visible flickering.

## Proposed changes

Only request post-paint notifications when the custom-draw rectangle has a valid, non-empty paint area. Empty paint regions now return CDRF_NEWFONT without requesting post-paint processing.

Eliminates flickering for owner-drawn TreeView text when double buffering is enabled, while preserving existing rendering behavior for valid paint regions.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0] Add opt-in native clipboard text fallback for WPF
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes dotnet/wpf#11968 together with the companion WPF port, dotnet/wpf#12125.

Main companion port: dotnet/winforms#15413.

## Proposed changes

- Port dotnet/winforms#15370 from `release/10.0` to `release/11.0`, including both source commits (`2f32164f6`, `5fb8ee647`) with cherry-pick provenance.
- Add default-disabled native clipboard text fallback for WPF, preserving managed custom-payload identity and protected typed retrieval. WinForms remains opted out.
- Support the opt-in fallback on .NET Framework as well as modern .NET, using instance OLE services and composed-data-object factories where static/default interface implementations are unavailable. Enable the shared fallback regressions on Framework and add recovered-managed-COM tests for enabled/disabled policy with typed and legacy sources. Normalize the added WinForms test's encoding.
- Require `SupportsTypedData` on both targets and implement it explicitly in concrete classes, removing the default interface body and Framework-only property guards. Public `DataObject` uses an explicit internal interface implementation, so no public API is added.

<!-- We are in TELL-MODE the following section must be completed -->

## Customer Impact

- Enables WPF to recover Windows plain-text synthesis when managed sources disable automatic conversion.
- Preserves existing WinForms clipboard behavior and default-disabled Framework behavior; Framework shared-core consumers can explicitly opt into text fallback.

## Regression? 

- Yes: supports the fix for the .NET 10 WPF regression. No intentional WinForms behavior change.

## Risk

- Low for WinForms, which remains opted out. Moderate for opted-in consumers: shared composition/retrieval paths change, restricted to exact-case Text, UnicodeText, and OEMText. Typed reads never directly fall back to legacy getters.

Issues.Title: WFO3011/WFO3012: Suggested VB fixes can introduce build errors and change runtime behavior
Issues.Body:
Helllo,

At DevExpress, we maintain a significant amount of Visual Basic code across our products and published materials. We've noticed that the newly introduced VB diagnostics affect a substantial portion of this code, including code in demos, project templates, and product documentation.

While testing .NET 11 RC2, we encountered several issues with the new WinForms Designer analyzers, particularly **WFO3011** and **WFO3012** (as well as WFO3001).

Given the number of affected places, reviewing and fixing everything within a reasonable timeframe would be challenging. More importantly, some of the suggested fixes are not safe to apply mechanically.

We have prepared four minimal repro projects demonstrating the issues: [WinForms-VB-Analyzer-Sample-Issues.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34684359/WinForms-VB-Analyzer-Sample-Issues.zip)

## Problems identified

### 1. Backing field collision (WFO3011 → BC31060)

WFO3011 suggests changing a regular component field to `WithEvents`:

```vb
Private button1 As System.Windows.Forms.Button
```

However, `WithEvents` makes the VB compiler generate a hidden `_button1` backing field. If the user partial class already contains a member with that name, the build fails with **BC31060**.

### 2. Setter collision (WFO3011 → BC31060)

A similar issue occurs if the class already contains a method named `set_button1`. The compiler-generated setter accessor conflicts with the existing method, resulting in **BC31060**.

### 3. Generic event handler (WFO3012 → BC32080)

Consider this valid VB event subscription:

```vb
AddHandler button1.Click, AddressOf HandleButtonClick(Of Integer)
```

WFO3012 suggests replacing `AddHandler` with a `Handles` clause. However, VB does not allow generic methods to be used as `Handles` event handlers, resulting in **BC32080**.

The workaround is to introduce a non-generic forwarding handler manually.

### 4. Event subscription timing changes (WFO3012 → silent behavior change)

This is the most concerning issue because the suggested fix builds successfully but changes runtime behavior.

With `AddHandler` at the end of `InitializeComponent`, the event subscription happens after component properties have been initialized.

With `Handles`, the handler is subscribed as soon as the field is assigned. Consequently, property setters executed later in `InitializeComponent` can trigger the handler during initialization.

In our repro, the handler is invoked once after applying the suggested fix, whereas it is never invoked with the original code.

We encountered this in one of our project templates: after the mechanical fix, a navigation panel becomes hidden when it should be visible.

## Why this matters

Both `AddHandler` inside `InitializeComponent` and private component fields without `WithEvents` are legitimate, long-standing VB patterns. They are used by code generators, third-party designers, serializers, and existing applications.

Many VB WinForms applications have 15+ years of accumulated code. For their developers, upgrading to .NET 11 could mean fixing hundreds of build errors, manually reviewing affected forms, and re-testing initialization behavior.

The four cases above demonstrate why this migration cannot be handled safely through a bulk replacement or an automatic code fix.

## Suggested changes

We would appreciate reconsideration of the default severity and applicability of these diagnostics:

1. **Make WFO3011 and WFO3012 warnings or suggestions by default** for existing projects, rather than errors that break the build after a simple TFM change. Alternatively, consider enabling them as errors only for new projects.
2. **Account for cases where the suggested fixes are unsafe**, including generated member name collisions, generic event handlers, and changes to event subscription timing.
3. **Document the migration implications**, including behavioral differences and how developers can opt out of these diagnostics, in the .NET 11 breaking changes documentation.

We understand the goals behind the new Designer analyzers and want to support more predictable Designer serialization. However, we believe this should not come at the cost of breaking otherwise valid existing VB applications or silently changing their behavior.



We previously had a [similar discussion regarding WFO1000](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/issues/12476) and appreciated the team's willingness to revisit its scope. We hope we can find a similarly practical solution here.

Issues.Title: [release/10.0] Fix issue 15213: Bitmap finalized during Image.Save(Stream, ImageFormat) leaks native GDI+ memory
Issues.Body:
Backport of #15254 to release/10.0

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/issues/15213

## Proposed changes

Within `CoreImageExtensions.Save(this IImage image, Stream stream, ...)` of `System.Private.Windows.GdiPlus`, wrap `GdipSaveImageToStream` in a try/finally block and call `GC.KeepAlive(image)` in the finally block.

## Customer Impact

The correction avoids abnormal native memory growth in `Save(Stream, ImageFormat)` under high-pressure/specific GC timings, reducing memory risks and potential stability issues in long-duration or batch image processing scenarios.

The impact on existing behavioral compatibility is minimal (only extending object survival to the end of the method), and should not change functional results or introduce visible behavioral differences.

## Regression? 

- Yes - regression PR: #10783 or #10784

- Manual
- Unit tests

- Mini

Issues.Title: Raise FormClosed once when the owner closes a modal dialog
Issues.Body:
Fixes #2451

## Proposed changes

- Let the modal message loop finish without raising close events again after the owner has raised them.
- Reset close state at the start of each modal run and let the legacy `Closing` handler participate in cancellation before the owner commits the close.
- Ignore synchronous nonmodal `WM_CLOSE` reentry while committed close events and disposal are being dispatched. Restore that temporary state in `finally`, allowing retry after a handler exception and allowing a new modal run started by a close handler.

## Customer Impact

An owner-driven modal close raises the child's `FormClosed` with `FormOwnerClosing` once. Calling `owner.Close()` again from a closed handler no longer repeats the committed close notifications or empties the owned-form list during iteration, which could cause `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` when the owner has multiple owned windows.

## Regression?

The original issue dates back to .NET Core 3.0 and .NET Framework 4.7.2.

## Risk

The change affects modal close sequencing. Legacy `Closing` now runs before an owner-driven modal close commits, where it can still cancel. The reentry guard is limited to active nonmodal closed-event dispatch; it does not intercept session-query/end-session messages or the close of a new modal run.

## Test methodology

- Added source regression coverage for owner close, both cancellation events, overlapping-close reuse, reentry from modal/owner closed handlers with multiple owned forms, session-query cancellation, handler-exception retry, and reopening a modal run from a closed callback.
- [dotnet-winforms CI build 1674968](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1674968) succeeded on `9738f6fd`: x64/x86/arm64 Debug and Release source builds passed with zero compiler warnings or errors. All four x64/x86 unit-test legs and four integration-test legs passed: 90,882 passed, zero failed, and 324 Other. Arm64 test execution is skipped by that pipeline; its two missing-test-XML publication warnings are expected. All eight GitHub checks, including CLA, passed.
- Private-desktop equivalent-IL probes on .NET 10.0.12 also passed all 38 after-fix scenarios. An independent reviewer separately verified exception recovery, nested end-session state restoration, modal reopening, and all ten added source-test rows in a focused host. These supplement the source-built CI results above.
- CI exposed a namespace-shadowing error in the added timer test. The test now uses `global::System.Windows.Forms.Timer`; the one-line correction received independent review and is included in the successful source build. `git diff --check` passed.

## Test environment

Windows 11 x64, .NET 10.0.12 for isolated probes; upstream Windows source CI as linked above.

Issues.Title: [Suggestion] Shorten ToggleSwitch state-transition animations
Issues.Body:
### Background and motivation

The ToggleSwitch state-transition animation can feel too slow, making the control feel less responsive to user input. The feedback on PR #15270 suggests shortening state-transition animations.

This proposal is limited to the ToggleSwitch appearance used by CheckBox and RadioButton. It does not include their standard appearances or other button controls.

AnimatedToggleSwitchRenderer currently uses a 300 ms animation duration. We propose evaluating approximately 150 ms as an initial candidate to improve responsiveness while preserving the existing easing and smooth transitions.

The change should preserve continuous motion during rapid or reverse toggling and respect system settings that disable animations. Since the renderer shares its animation duration with hover and focus transitions, those interactions should also be validated.

### Will this feature affect UI controls?

Yes. This change affects only CheckBox and RadioButton controls using Appearance.ToggleSwitch, shortening their visual state-transition animations.

No changes to layout, sizing, public APIs, or logical checked-state behavior are intended. Standard CheckBox and RadioButton appearances and other UI controls will remain unaffected.

Because AnimatedToggleSwitchRenderer shares its animation duration with hover and focus transitions, those visual effects may also become faster and should be validated. System settings that disable animations will continue to be respected.
